Measured on this host's own MPSGraph and compared cell for cell by tests/backports/host/mpsgraph/run.sh in a process of its own: 9 cases over both forms and their result shapes, every cell and every shape byte-identical to the release (gather_slice checks=9 failures=0 recorded=0 over 44 cells). Three shapes the release refuses, each with its own words and each a question refusals.m asks in a process of its own: a start past the end of the axis ("start value 9 does not fit dimension size (4)"), a length that runs past it ("length value 9 does not fit within the dimension size (4) with start value (2)"), a stride of zero ("stride cannot be 0"), and a result of no elements, which the release BUILDS (the shape line prints 2x0) and then cannot make an NDArray for ("device may not be nil", MPSNDArray.mm:759). Each axis is chosen on its own, because a pad is applied to every axis at once. TWO OF THE SEVEN MODES ARE REFUSED BY THE RELEASE, with its own words, "Unsupported paddingMode", after it has built the result tensor - so MPSGraphPaddingModePeriodic and MPSGraphPaddingModeAntiPeriodic are raised where the graph is built. The clamp, the zero and the constant answer any padding at all. A pad of a RANK OF THREE answers, and the earlier text of this row was wrong: it said the release refuses one in every mode, and that was a measurement of this repository's own question asked into the wrong shape - a destination of the OPERAND's 96 bytes where the result is a 4x5x6 of 480. Asked into a destination of the RESULT's shape a 2x3x4 of (1 ... 24) padded by one at each end of every axis answers a 4x5x6 in every mode, measured, and the clamp and the symmetric answer the same bytes there because one element of padding on an axis of two or more is where the two mirrors and the clamp agree; refusals.txt now records what the narrower destination really does, which is per mode and per rank (pad-destination-narrower-rank3-clamp is refused, pad-destination-narrower-rank3-constant and pad-destination-narrower-rank2 answer). THE CALLER'S DESTINATION DOES NOT DECIDE THE COUNT - it decides how much of the answer is written, and this family writes the WHOLE destination: the rows the answer does not reach are a WRITTEN ZERO (measured over a destination filled with the byte 0xbd: five non-zero elements into seventy-two rows leaves no 0xbd in any of them), an answer of exactly ONE row is written into EVERY row of it (element 71 alone into twelve rows and into two hundred, twelve copies of (2,3,5) and two hundred of them), a destination with FEWER rows than the answer has cuts the answer short, and the rows are written rank cells apart in the destination's OWN last extent (a destination of shape 3x4 keeps its fourth cell and one of rank one has the three cells of the answer written into the front of it). A destination of NO ROWS is the one shape the release cannot be given: it goes down inside its own NDArray with "buffer is not large enough. Must be 12 bytes" (MPSNDArray.mm:893), and with a buffer of no bytes at all one line earlier and another of its own sentences ("Error: device may not be nil", MPSNDArray.mm:759) - refusals.txt's nonzero-destination-no-rows, nonzero-result-shape and nonzero-destination-five-rows. FOUR CELLS OF A SEVENTY-TWO-ROW DESTINATION ARE NOT THIS OPERATION'S ANSWER AT ALL and are recorded in recorded-cells.txt with both runs' bytes: the release writes 3 at cell 197 of a count of two, 2 there of a count of three and 3 at 203 and 2 at 206 of a count of five, determinately (five processes of one case each print the same bytes) and neither coordinate is one of any element of the operand; the port writes the operation's own answer there, which is a zero. The run's verdict line is "gather_nonzero checks=24 failures=0 recorded=4" over 2106 cells in 51 cases with the red control differing from the release in 22 of the 51, and facts/MetalPerformanceShadersGraph/Core.md carries every measurement.
